---
applyTo: "{Makefile,pyproject.toml,conftest.py,.semgrepignore,tools/**,.github/workflows/**}"
description: "The CI and test gates are never softened. A failing gate means fix the code."
---

# Gates

`make check` is the single gate (S5 11.1): `deps-sync` and `tools-sync` (the pinned security binaries, which the gate proofs also use), then `py-check` (ruff check, ruff format --check, mypy strict, no-rigging, silent-except, roles, cost-parity, ratchet, deps-policy, push-clean, pytest `-W error --full-gate` with the 90% branch-coverage floor, scope-coverage, diff-cover 90%), then `sec-check` (bandit two passes, Semgrep, CodeQL security-extended, gitleaks, TruffleHog, pip-audit `--require-hashes`, osv-scanner, licence gate). CI calls the same make targets for `py-check` (against the pre-change base from `tools/ci_base_ref.sh`), the Python scans and `make gitleaks`; TruffleHog, osv-scanner, CodeQL and a second gitleaks pass run in CI through official Actions pinned to full commit SHAs, at the scanner versions `tools/ensure_tools.sh` pins (`tools/tests/test_ci_workflows.py` holds the two in step). Workflows carry no path filter.

- Thresholds live in `tools/gates/ratchet.toml` and only get stricter. Change a threshold in its source file and in the ratchet in the same commit, and only upward.
- What each gate looks at (ruff, mypy, coverage, pytest, bandit, Semgrep and CodeQL scopes) is pinned by `tools/tests/test_gate_scope.py`: every `[tool.ruff]`, `[tool.mypy]`, `[tool.pytest]` and `[tool.coverage]` table must equal its pin exactly, so any added ignore, disabled error code, `addopts` selection or exclusion is a visible, reviewed change to that test. `make test` runs pytest with `--full-gate`: a selection option, a deselected test or a never-collected test file fails it.
- Suppressions are forbidden: `noqa`, `type: ignore`, inline `# mypy:` config, `no_type_check`, `nosec`, `nosemgrep`, `gitleaks:allow`, `.gitleaksignore` and gitleaks config entries, `trufflehog:ignore`, `osv-scanner.toml` ignores, `--ignore-vuln`, any warning filter whose action is not `error` or any other use of `warnings` beyond emitting (judged on the Python syntax tree, so keyword, multiline, aliased and reflective forms count), the `recwarn` fixture, a competing tool config (`mypy.ini`, `setup.cfg`, `tox.ini`, `pytest.ini`, `ruff.toml`, `.coveragerc`) or a gate `[tool.*]` table outside the root `pyproject.toml`, `# isort: skip`, `pragma: no cover`, skip/xfail, `continue-on-error`. The only exception is a proven false positive in `tools/gates/suppressions-allowlist.toml`: one file, one marker, the exact line, and a reason. Adding an entry is a gate change and needs its own review.
- Never add `continue-on-error` (the scan reads YAML as YAML: only a plain `false` passes), remove a `needs:`, lower a timeout floor, or broaden an exclude.
- A new gate ships with a gateproof test (`@pytest.mark.gateproof`) that proves it fails on a seeded defect.
- Lifted files are recorded in `ATTRIBUTIONS.md` (source path, commit, sha256, changes) and pass every gate like new code.
